evidence:
Both papers treat Fourier frequencies as the learned units, but neither defines a feature as a frequency with nonzero logit amplitude. "As in" is therefore too strong.

**Nanda et al., ICLR 2023** (arXiv 2301.05217; PDF fetched, header says "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023").
- Sec. 4.1: "W_E is sparse in the Fourier basis -- it only has significant nonnegligible norm at 6 frequencies. Of these frequencies, only 5 appear to be used significantly in later parts of the model (k in {14,35,41,42,52}). We dub these the key frequencies of the model."
- Fig. 3 caption: "W_L is well-approximated by the 5 key frequencies". Sec. 4.4 uses ablations (restricted and excluded loss).
- The paper never calls frequencies "features". The only occurrence of the word is "some feature of the loss landscape".
- Its criterion is empirical and thresholded, and it excludes a frequency that has nonzero embedding norm. So it is not "exactly nonzero means feature". It does match the idea of an amplitude measured at the logit level (in W_L).

**Morwani et al., ICLR 2024** (arXiv 2311.07568v2; PDF and HTML fetched).
- Abstract: "analytically characterize the features learned ... the trained networks utilize Fourier features to perform modular addition".
- Informal theorem and Thm 7: "For every neuron, there exists a frequency such that the Fourier spectra of the input and output weight vectors are supported only on that frequency" and "at least one neuron in the network uses this frequency".
- Here a feature is the Fourier structure of the weights, and "uses a frequency" is defined per neuron by spectral support. That is close in spirit to A_j>0, but it is a different definition.

Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/c9-feature-definition/CHECK.md.
recommended_change: In approach.tex:27, replace "a frequency with $A_j>0$ is a \emph{feature}, as in \citet{nanda2023progress,morwani2024feature}" with: "a frequency with $A_j>0$ is a \emph{feature}. This is the exact counterpart of the empirical `key frequencies' of \citet{nanda2023progress} and of the frequencies that neurons `use' in \citet{morwani2024feature}." Optionally add a footnote: trained networks have small nonzero amplitudes at every frequency, so the empirical count uses an ablation threshold (Nanda's protocol). Keep both existing citations.
